validity.recommendation: Replace the 292 km length with the operator's 357.7 km, or document what 292 means. Do not copy 29 bcm/y to each string: it is a system figure.
validity.researcher_notes: The line is real. The Belarus operator and the iSANS report both describe a two-thread line, and the Ukrainian operator history lists strings I, II and a third string (17.8 km, 1979), so GEM carries two of three strings. It is not a duplicate of P5938: the operator gives different lengths and years for the two strings. Problems: the sheet length of 292 km is not supported (operator table says 357.7 km for string I, 366.7 km for string II). The 29 bcm/y is a system figure on both rows. The iSANS report puts the whole system at about 30 bcm a year. The Urengoy fuel source has no support, and the field began producing after the recorded start. The operator cell lacks the Ukrainian operator.

fills.researcher_notes: No source found for a construction year of 1974 for string I. The Ukrainian operator history table lists only the 1976 commissioning. Searched in Ukrainian and Russian.

The iSANS report (2023) gives about 30 bcm a year for the whole twin-thread Ivatsevichi-Dolina line. That is a system figure, not a figure for one string, so it is not used as a ref for this row. At 1220 mm one string would carry about 15 to 20 bcm a year. No per-string capacity found. Searched in Russian and Ukrainian.

fills.researcher_notes: Three publishers agree on 1220 mm: the iSANS report (2023), the Gazprom Transgaz Belarus activities page (2023 capture), and the Ukrainian operator history table, which gives 1220 mm for string I. The names match the sheet closely.

No source found that names Urengoy gas as the supply for this line. Note the Urengoy field first produced gas in 1978, after the recorded start. The Ukrainian operator history says this line began as a reversal of the older Dashava-Minsk flow. Searched in Russian and Ukrainian.

fills.researcher_notes: The sheet says 292 km. The Ukrainian operator history table gives 357.7 km for string I of Ivatsevichi-Dolina. The sheet value looks wrong. It may be half of a 146 km figure that appears in other sources for each string, but no source found states 292. Caution: it is not clear whether the table figure covers the whole run from Ivatsevichi or only part. The other string is given as 366.7 km, so the two strings differ. Proposed as a change with a spec concern. The geometry on the sheet measures about 480 km.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Newest dated evidence found is the 2023 Gazprom Transgaz Belarus page, covering the Belarus section. A source dated 2024 or later for the Ukrainian section was not found. Russian transit ended on 2025-01-01, but the line also links Belarus and Ukraine and has reverse-flow potential. No source says it is shut. Status stays operating with low certainty.

cross_row_leads.facts: Operator history table: string II of Ivatsevichi-Dolina is 366.7 km, 1220 mm, commissioned 1977 (sheet has 292 km and 1981). The table also lists a third string (17.8 km, 1220 mm, 1979) and a 23.8 km section in 1977. GEM has no row for a third string; route to discovery.

summary: "Real, not a duplicate of P5938; length 292 km and 29 bcm/y unsupported (operator table 357.7 km); fuel unresolved"
